newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Lebed heckled in Duma over Chechnya.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Lebed heckled in Duma over Chechnya.

text.p: Russian security chief Alexander Lebed was jeered as a "traitor" in the State Duma lower chamber of parliament on Wednesday and left the chamber in frustration after trying to defend agreements that ended the Chechnya war.

The blunt-speaking Lebed, whose peace agreements were condemned by some deputies as a humiliating capitulation that could lead to the break-up of Russia, also clashed with Interior Minister Anatoly Kulikov.

Lebed, who has accused Kulikov of being among those responsible for the 21-month Chechnya conflict, told the largely hostile chamber that 80,000 to 100,000 people had been killed since Russia sent troops to Chechnya in December 1994.
"We must not allow the resumption of this bloody armed conflict," the Security Council secretary said.
Lebed rejected accusations that the agreement, which called for Russian troop withdrawals and postponed a decision on Chechnya's status for five years, would violate Russia's territorial integrity.
But some deputies opposed to the deal jeered and shouted "shame, shame" and "traitor".
After delivering his report and listening to a barrage of criticism from subsequent speakers, including Kulikov, Lebed tried to defend his position but eventually gave up in despair.
"Respected deputies, thank you," he snapped before pushing his way to the exit through a mass of journalists and deputies.
Kulikov, in a 10-minute speech just after Lebed's report, won thunderous applause after describing the peace deal as a humiliating step towards the disintegration of Russia.
He said the Chechens were violating the agreements. "These documents are not only being violated but they are being trampled on in the most rude way at every step," he said.
"The Chechen separatists are behaving in such a way as if the question of Chechnya seceding has already been decided."

The heated debate in the Duma, dominated by communists and nationalists, came on the eve of a new round of peace talks in Moscow. Chechen separatist leader Zelimkhan Yandarbiyev, due to arrive on Thursday, was sticking by demands for independence, Interfax news agency said.
But Lebed, who in August unsuccessfully called on President Boris Yeltsin to sack Kulikov, denied that Russia was quitting Chechnya.
"Russia is not leaving Chechnya and should not leave it," he said. "We have put an end to something that could bring shame (on Russia) for many long years to come," he added.

Yeltsin, who has backed Kulikov but given cautious approval of Lebed's peace initiative, is due to meet Lebed on Thursday for their first talks since the security chief forged the deal with the rebels on August 31 in the southern town of Khasavyurt.
Lebed appealed to parliament for economic aid for Chechnya, asking "which is the better investment -- war or peace".
But Kulikov and other speakers described the peace accords as "a cover for most humiliating unilateral concessions".

"The Khasavyurt agreements amount to the complete capitulation of Russia...The ambitions of the separatists are completely satisfied," said Viktor Ilyukhin, the communist head of the Duma's security committee.
Lebed scorned those who demanded that the Chechen rebels be disarmed, the war ended and Russia's integrity preserved.
"And in their opinion this should be done by purely peaceful means," he said sarcastically. "I will not comment on this. You either need a magician, a golden fish or something like this."
He said the Khasavyurt deal was only the start of a long process that would satisfy the interests of both sides.
